Synopsis:
MMF assets have hit a record $13.5T globally (~$8T US), up 58-65% since Dec 2022. What began as a rate-driven yield play has structurally evolved: institutional defensive positioning and corporate cash from AI-related capital raises (tech giants issued $121B+ in debt in 2025; SpaceX/Alphabet/SK Hynix raised ~$200B in equity in 2026) are now the dominant inflow drivers. The key thesis is that MMFs are no longer just "cash on the sidelines" waiting to rotate into risk assets — they represent strategic, semi-permanent allocations. This reframes how market participants should interpret this liquidity pool.
